pages.text: There were many shells on the sandy shore. Each time the water came in and went out, new shells appeared. Taro and Mumu collected them.
"Let's make a big circle of shells!" "Okay. Let's collect ten each!" They planned to sit inside the circle.
Mumu set down shells one at a time. Quick-handed Taro picked up two at once. Each time he said, "One!" he set down two.
Taro counted. One, two, three... ten. He had twenty shells.
Mumu counted. One, two, three... ten. Mumu had ten shells.
"I've got them all!" "Me, too!" They met with shells in their arms.
Taro had far more shells. Mumu's eyes widened. "Why do you have so many?"
Taro counted again to show Mumu. "One!" He put down two. Mumu called, "You're putting down two for every one!"
They poured all the shells onto the sand. Thirty shells! They laid them out in a circle.
The circle grew very big. They went inside and flopped down. Even with their legs stretched out, their feet could not reach the shells.
